# `clear_batch_stack`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Mark the batch stack state as cleared while no batch worker is running.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc9f20, ClearBatchStack @0x3a66f0 (64-bit build) |

When the batch worker is idle, sets a cached clear flag in the batch status. It does not synchronously delete input files or results and does not zero every counter. No camera or mount precondition and no wait beyond the running check. No request parameters are read.

Side effects: Sets the cached clear flag in the batch stack status.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"clear_batch_stack"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 259 | The batch worker is running | `stack is already running` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No other ordinary local error is reachable.

## Example

Request, clear:

```json
{"id":151,"method":"clear_batch_stack"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"clear_batch_stack","result":0,"code":0,"id":151}
```

Reply, batch-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"clear_batch_stack","error":"stack is already running","code":259,"id":152}
```
